entities.name: L-citrulline
observations: Oral supplementation at 2.5 g/kg body weight reduced diet-induced hepatic triglycerides and inflammatory liver markers in female C57BL/6J mice.
In a separate progression model, oral supplementation attenuated early diet-induced NAFLD/NASH progression; benefit was abolished by intestinal arginase inhibition with NOHA.

entities.name: NAFLD
observations: In female C57BL/6J mice, a Western-style diet induced NAFLD, while concurrent oral L-citrulline reduced hepatic triglycerides, hepatic neutrophils, and PAI-1 protein.
In a fat-, fructose-, and cholesterol-rich diet model, oral L-citrulline attenuated progression of early NAFLD/NASH after induction; a clear antifibrotic effect was not established.

entities.name: PMID:27496089
observations: Female 6–8-week-old C57BL/6J mice received a liquid Western-style diet with or without oral L-citrulline at 2.5 g/kg body weight for 6 weeks; citrulline reduced hepatic triglycerides, hepatic neutrophils, and PAI-1 protein versus Western-style diet alone.

entities.name: PMID:33550112
observations: Female C57BL/6J mice underwent 8 weeks of fat-, fructose-, and cholesterol-rich diet induction followed by 5 weeks with or without oral L-citrulline at 2.5 g/kg body weight; citrulline attenuated early NAFLD/NASH progression, and NOHA abolished the protective effect.
